Explanation: The core value unit in this case is a business chat: a private conversation in which a customer can ask, buy, receive updates or get support while a business can reply or send approved messages at scale.
Meta owns WhatsApp and controls the messaging infrastructure, Business Platform, pricing, templates, encryption design, safety rules and commercial surfaces around the private network.
Meta has to grow revenue from WhatsApp without undermining the private, reliable messaging experience that made the network valuable in the first place.
Business messaging, click-to-message advertising and new Updates-tab products create revenue around a user base that still receives the core messaging service for free.
Too much commercial messaging, scams or unclear data use could damage trust, increase blocks and make users less willing to keep WhatsApp at the center of daily communication.
WhatsApp routes business conversations and can charge for eligible business messaging while keeping ordinary personal communication free to users.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Intent / Consent — Customers initiate chats, reply, grant or withdraw consent, block or report businesses and generate the demand signals that keep business messaging useful. | → Consumer · Messages / Calls — WhatsApp securely delivers business messages, calls and interactive flows while keeping the core customer experience inside the familiar app. | ← Provider · Messages / Fees — Businesses submit replies or approved message templates through WhatsApp and pay Meta for eligible paid messaging at scale. | → Provider · Delivery / Reach — WhatsApp gives businesses access to customers, message delivery, business identity, automation and increasingly AI, voice and campaign tools. | ← Partner · Systems / Tools — Integrators connect CRM, support, commerce and automation systems to the WhatsApp Business layer. | → Partner · APIs / Access — Meta provides APIs, platform access, technical rules and business-messaging capabilities that partners can embed into client solutions.

Explanation: WhatsApp combines end-to-end encryption with opt-in, template, quality and blocking rules for business messages. Personal chats, calls and groups are not used to determine ads in the Updates tab.
Businesses can bring people into WhatsApp through click-to-message ads, while Ads in Status create a separate discovery surface in the Updates tab rather than inside personal chats.
Meta operates encrypted messaging, message delivery, abuse prevention, business APIs, template review, quality systems and increasingly AI-assisted business support.
WhatsApp combines a global communication network, identity and contact graphs, encrypted infrastructure, Business APIs and Meta’s wider advertising and AI systems.
Consumers in this bounded model are WhatsApp users who start or receive conversations with businesses. They sit inside a much larger private-messaging network and do not pay Meta to use the core app.
Customers want to ask a question, get support, receive an update, book or buy without leaving the familiar messaging app they already use for personal communication.
A business chat can be faster than email, phone queues or a separate app and can keep confirmations, support and follow-up in one familiar conversation.
Customers risk unwanted promotions, impersonation, scams and message overload if businesses can reach them too aggressively or without clear consent.
Customers start chats, ask questions, reply to messages, request support, browse offers or complete actions through a private business conversation.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Intent / Consent — Customers initiate chats, reply, grant or withdraw consent, block or report businesses and generate the demand signals that keep business messaging useful. | ← Owner · Messages / Calls — WhatsApp securely delivers business messages, calls and interactive flows while keeping the core customer experience inside the familiar app.

Explanation: People can choose whether to engage, block or report businesses, and WhatsApp uses user feedback and policy enforcement to limit low-quality messaging.
Customers access businesses through WhatsApp itself, links, QR codes, click-to-message ads, business discovery and increasingly search inside the app.
Customers send messages, voice notes and media, make calls and interact with menus, forms, AI agents or other business workflows.
Customers contribute their intent, account identity, conversation context and explicit actions, while the contents of personal chats remain protected by end-to-end encryption.

Providers are businesses that supply service, information, commerce and support through WhatsApp. Small firms may use the Business app; larger organizations can integrate the Business Platform into their own systems.
Businesses want to answer questions, send useful updates, support purchases and maintain customer relationships in a channel people already check frequently.
WhatsApp can convert existing mobile reach into support efficiency, repeat engagement, leads and sales without requiring customers to install a separate business app.
Businesses must manage message costs, templates, opt-in, quality ratings, staffing and the risk that customers block them if messages feel irrelevant or excessive.
Businesses respond to customer messages and can send approved utility, authentication or marketing templates through the Business Platform.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Messages / Fees — Businesses submit replies or approved message templates through WhatsApp and pay Meta for eligible paid messaging at scale. | ← Owner · Delivery / Reach — WhatsApp gives businesses access to customers, message delivery, business identity, automation and increasingly AI, voice and campaign tools.

Explanation: Business-initiated messages are constrained by approved template categories, opt-in expectations, quality feedback and commerce or messaging policies.
Businesses use the WhatsApp Business app, Cloud API/Business Platform and connected business tools to manage conversations at different scales.
Businesses answer customers, send order or account updates, run campaigns, automate service, make product recommendations and increasingly add voice or AI support.
Businesses contribute product and service information, catalogs, support teams, transaction data, customer permissions and operational systems that make the conversation useful.

Partners are CRM, helpdesk, commerce and solution providers that connect WhatsApp to enterprise systems. They are not the business offering itself; they make large-scale customer messaging, automation and workflow integration practical.
Integrators help businesses connect WhatsApp conversations to CRM, commerce, support, identity and automation systems already used inside the company.
WhatsApp gives software and solution providers access to a large business-messaging market and creates demand for implementation, automation and workflow services.
Partners must keep up with API changes, messaging policies, template rules, security requirements and client-specific integration complexity.
Partners connect business systems to WhatsApp, manage workflows and help clients operate compliant messaging at scale.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Systems / Tools — Integrators connect CRM, support, commerce and automation systems to the WhatsApp Business layer. | ← Owner · APIs / Access — Meta provides APIs, platform access, technical rules and business-messaging capabilities that partners can embed into client solutions.

Explanation: Partner implementations must respect WhatsApp Business policy, permissions, data handling, approved use cases and technical requirements.
Integrators work through WhatsApp Business APIs, Meta business tooling and connected enterprise systems rather than through the consumer chat interface alone.
Partners implement inboxes, CRM sync, routing, bots, commerce flows, reporting and other automation around WhatsApp conversations.
Integrators contribute software, implementation knowledge, connectors, support operations and enterprise relationships that extend WhatsApp into business workflows.
